exposure: early-life exposure to the 1959-1961 Chinese Great Famine
cohort: Survivors of the 1959-1961 Chinese Great Famine, across various birth cohorts and regions, represented by nationally representative data.
finding: Early-life exposure to the Chinese Great Famine significantly reduces emotional and eudaimonic subjective well-being fifty years later, especially among females, while evaluative subjective well-being remains unaffected.
